name: get_struct_state
reason: Excluded as no-behaviour: the body only returns _PyModule_GetState(module) behind an assert, which is nothing Python can see.

name: get_pylong
reason: getPylong (StructModel.lean:383-386, cited 112-134) follows the PyLong_Check / PyIndex_Check / struct.error branches. GetPylongLaw covers every PyO: the __index__ result, raises included, comes out unchanged, and an object without __index__ gets "required argument is not an integer". IntCodesRoundTrip covers the PyLong_Check branch. Gap: the DeprecationWarning that _PyNumber_Index gives for an int-subclass result is not modelled.

name: get_long
reason: Neither theorem pins PyLong_AsLong's OverflowError on an out-of-range int: IntCodesRoundTrip takes only in-range values and IndexRaises takes only non-overflow __index__ errors, so a getLong that wraps silently satisfies both.

name: get_ulong
reason: The negative-value message is wrong: the model says "can't convert negative int to unsigned" but Objects/longobject.c:786 says "can't convert negative value to unsigned int" (struct replaces it, so it is not visible). Nothing pins the negative or too-large OverflowError: a wrapping getUlong passes the round trip and IndexRaises.

name: get_longlong
reason: The overflow message is wrong: the model says "Python int too large to convert to C long long" but PyLong_AsLongLong goes through _PyLong_AsByteArray, which raises "int too big to convert" (longobject.c:1250; not visible through struct). Nothing pins the out-of-range branch.

name: get_ulonglong
reason: The overflow message is wrong: the model says "Python int too large to convert" but _PyLong_AsByteArray says "int too big to convert" (not visible through struct). Nothing pins the negative or too-large branch, so a wrapping conversion satisfies both theorems.

name: get_ssize_t
reason: PyLong_AsSsize_t's OverflowError is never stated: the round trip is in-range only and IndexRaises leaves out OverflowError, so a wrapping getSsizeT passes.

name: get_size_t
reason: The negative message is wrong: the model says "can't convert negative int to size_t" but longobject.c:830 says "can't convert negative value to size_t" (not visible). Nothing pins the negative or overflow branch.

name: unpack_halffloat
reason: ScalarByteOrder holds for any decoder, because both sides call the same pyFloatUnpack2Bits on leVal and beVal of the same bytes. A constant unpack_halffloat therefore passes, and the decoded value is pinned only by the .open HalfRoundTrip.

name: pack_halffloat
reason: FloatFailureReplaced pins the struct.error replacement and ScalarByteOrder pins the le flag, but nothing pins what PyFloat_Pack2 writes or when it overflows. A pack_halffloat that writes [0,0] on success passes, because HalfRoundTrip is .open.

name: unpack_float
reason: ScalarByteOrder holds for any decoder shared by luFloat and buFloat, so the PyFloat_Unpack4 value, including the sNaN handling, is unpinned. FloatRoundTrip, which would pin it, is .open.

name: unpack_double
reason: ScalarByteOrder relates luDouble and buDouble through the same helper, so `fun _ _ => float 0` satisfies it. No theorem says the result is the 8-byte pattern.

name: _range_error
reason: rangeError is (size_t)-1 >> ((8-size)*8), then ulargest>>1 and ~largest, with the same two format strings (316-343). RangeErrorBounds, decided over every integer entry of every table, says the message gives the documented range, so a wrong bound or sign fails. The 3.15 body is unchanged from the model.

name: nu_char
reason: runUnpack .nuChar is PyBytes_FromStringAndSize(p, 1). CharCode says every byte b unpacks to bytes([b]).

name: nu_byte
reason: signedOf 1 (leVal) is the signed-char read. IntCodesRoundTrip inverts np_byte on all 256 patterns, since the in-range twos images are every pattern, so unpack is pinned on every buffer.

name: nu_ubyte
reason: leVal of one byte is the unsigned-char read, and the round trip covers all 256 patterns.

name: nu_short
reason: memcpy into a short is signedOf 2 (leVal) on x86-64, and the round trip pins it on every 2-byte pattern in the native table (alignment 2) and in the post-swap little-endian table.

name: nu_ushort
reason: memcpy into an unsigned short is leVal, pinned on every pattern by the round trip.

name: nu_int
reason: memcpy into an int is signedOf 4, pinned on all 2**32 patterns by the round trip.

name: nu_uint
reason: PyLong_FromUnsignedLong of the 4-byte read is leVal, pinned by the round trip.

name: nu_long
reason: An 8-byte long on LP64 is signedOf 8, pinned on every pattern by the round trip.

name: nu_ulong
reason: An 8-byte unsigned long is leVal, pinned by the round trip.

name: nu_ssize_t
reason: PyLong_FromSsize_t of the 8-byte read is signedOf 8, pinned by the round trip.

name: nu_size_t
reason: PyLong_FromSize_t of the 8-byte read is leVal, pinned by the round trip.

name: nu_longlong
reason: signedOf 8, pinned by the round trip in the native table and in the post-swap little-endian q entry.

name: nu_ulonglong
reason: leVal of 8 bytes, pinned by the round trip.

name: nu_bool
reason: memcmp(p, &false, 1) is p.head? != some 0. BoolAnyNonzero says every byte b reads as b != 0, so a reader that tested == 1 would fail.

name: nu_halffloat
reason: The body only picks le=1 under PY_LITTLE_ENDIAN. ScalarByteOrder's pair (nuHalffloat, buHalffloat) says nu(p) = bu(reverse p), which fails if the wrapper passes le=0.

name: nu_float
reason: castFloatToDouble is the (double) cast, which quiets an sNaN. NativeFloatMatchesBig is refuted at 0x7f800001, which runs nu_float against bu_float, and bugs/textlibs-struct-native-float-snan.yaml exists.

name: nu_double
reason: The memcpy is leVal. ScalarByteOrder's pair (nuDouble, buDouble) pins it against bu_double on every 8-byte buffer.

name: nu_float_complex
reason: Two float reads are each widened by the cast. NativeComplexMatchesBig is refuted by the sNaN pair, which runs nu_float_complex against bu_float_complex, and its bug record (textlibs-struct-native-float-snan) exists.

name: nu_double_complex
reason: le8 0 and le8 8 are the double[2] memcpy. ComplexByteOrder's pair with buDoubleComplex says nu(p) = bu(swapParts 8 p) for every 16-byte buffer.

name: nu_void_p
reason: PyLong_FromVoidPtr reads unsigned (leVal). The round trip on 0..2**64-1 pins it on every pattern.

name: np_byte
reason: Neither the -128..127 check nor the OverflowError-to-RANGE_ERROR branch is pinned: IntCodesRoundTrip takes only in-range ints, so an np_byte that wraps 200 to 0xc8 satisfies every theorem that lists it.

name: np_ubyte
reason: The x < 0 || x > 255 range check and the overflow branch are unpinned, so a wrapping pack passes the round trip.

name: np_char
reason: runPack .npChar accepts only .bytes [b]. CharCode pins the byte for every b and the exact struct.error for every other value, bytearray and length 0 or 2 included, as PyBytes_Check rejects them.

name: np_short
reason: The SHRT_MIN/SHRT_MAX check and the overflow branch are not stated: only in-range values are, so a wrapping np_short passes.

name: np_ushort
reason: The 0..USHRT_MAX check, which here follows a signed get_long, is not pinned, so a wrapping pack passes the round trip.

name: np_int
reason: IndexOverflow pins the OverflowError-to-RANGE_ERROR branch, but the INT_MIN/INT_MAX check at 619-622, the one LP64 actually reaches, is unpinned: an np_int that skipped it and wrapped 2**31 would pass. The registry cites 576-579, which are np_short's lines; np_int's are 613-617.

name: np_uint
reason: The x > UINT_MAX check at 640-643 is unpinned, so a pack that truncates to 32 bits passes the round trip.

name: np_long
reason: The body's only branch, overflow to RANGE_ERROR, has no theorem: a pack that wraps out-of-range ints passes the in-range round trip.

name: np_ulong
reason: Negative and too-large values (the overflow to RANGE_ERROR branch) are not stated, so the round trip alone does not tell this apart from a wrapping pack.

name: np_ssize_t
reason: The overflow branch is unpinned, and only in-range values are stated.

name: np_size_t
reason: The negative and overflow branch is unpinned, and only in-range values are stated.

name: np_longlong
reason: The 3.15 body gives its own LLONG_MIN/LLONG_MAX message (708-716), and the model copies it, but no theorem reaches the overflow branch or the message.

name: np_ulonglong
reason: The model copies the 3.15 ULLONG_MAX message (726-733), but no theorem covers the negative or too-large branch.

name: np_bool
reason: BoolRaises pins the IsTrue failure, but BoolCode only asks for some w that unpacks to the truth value. A pack writing [] or [2] for True passes, so neither the written byte 0x01 nor the 1-byte length is pinned.

name: np_halffloat
reason: The body only calls pack_halffloat with le=1. ScalarByteOrder's pair (npHalffloat, bpHalffloat) says the native bytes are the reverse of >e's for every value or the same error, which pins the flag.

name: np_float
reason: The body is PyFloat_AsDouble, then the struct.error replacement (FloatFailureReplaced), then PyFloat_Pack4 with le=1. NativeFloatPack says its result is the reversed bp_float result, or the same error, for every value.

name: np_double
reason: The memcpy of the double is ordered le 8. ScalarByteOrder pins it against bp_double (PyFloat_Pack8 with le=0) for every value, and FloatFailureReplaced pins the error replacement.

name: np_float_complex
reason: The model mirrors the unchecked (float) casts of 792-793 before the error test. StdComplexOrderAgree is refuted by 1e300: <F, which uses this routine after the swap, succeeds where >F raises. bugs/textlibs-struct-le-complex-float-overflow.yaml exists, and it duplicates gh-156865.

name: np_double_complex
reason: leBytes 8 of each part is the double[2] memcpy. packDN_order in ComplexByteOrder says the native D bytes are bp_double_complex's with each part reversed, for every value.

name: np_void_p
reason: The negative, AsLong and AsUnsignedLong split follows PyLong_AsVoidPtr (longobject.c:1525-1551). The round trip pins success, and PIndexLikeInt, refuted at 2**64, pins the raw OverflowError that s_pack_internal rewrites only for an exact int. bugs/textlibs-struct-void-p-index-overflow.yaml exists.

name: bu_short
reason: The shift loop and the sign extension (x ^ 0x8000) - 0x8000 are signExtC over beVal. IntCodesRoundTrip with bp_int pins them on every 2-byte pattern.

name: bu_int
reason: signExtC 0x80000000 over beVal, pinned on every 4-byte pattern by the round trip for both >i and >l.

name: bu_uint
reason: The loop over f->size is beVal, which the round trip pins for H, I and L.

name: bu_longlong
reason: signExtC 0x8000000000000000 over beVal, pinned by the round trip with bp_longlong on every 8-byte pattern.

name: bu_ulonglong
reason: beVal over 8 bytes, pinned by the round trip.

name: bu_halffloat
reason: The body is unpack_halffloat with le=0. ScalarByteOrder's pairs with luHalffloat and nuHalffloat pin that flag.

name: bu_float
reason: The body is unpack_float with le=0. The luFloat/buFloat pair of ScalarByteOrder pins it on every 4-byte buffer.

name: bu_double
reason: The body is unpack_double with le=0. ScalarByteOrder pins it against luDouble and against nu_double's memcpy.

name: bu_float_complex
reason: Two PyFloat_Unpack4 calls at p and p+4. ComplexByteOrder's pair with lu_float_complex pins it on every 8-byte buffer, and the refuted NativeComplexMatchesBig also runs it.

name: bu_double_complex
reason: Two Unpack8 calls at p and p+8. ComplexByteOrder pins it against lu_double_complex and nu_double_complex on every 16-byte buffer.

name: bu_bool
reason: *p != 0 is p.head? != some 0. BoolAnyNonzero says every byte b reads as b != 0.
